scope: Exactly six complete new exact-position values, read against every clause of the supplied English source. Modern technical-loan register evaluated without treating standard-language readability as proof of target-language idiom. No repository/source edits and no acceptance of earlier review claims.

help_semantic_clause_audit.interpretation_limit: Audit records recoverable intended meaning; a true item does not clear a linguistic hold.

R1.scope: NINJAL Shuri Okinawan dictionary workbook checked locally against draft reference hashes. Verb entries distinguish put in from enter; selection, setting, overlap and expansion entries inspected. Reconsideration also directly inspected workbook rows 90/3596/11918/10317 for noun-adjectival attributive -na; ciNtu row1748 is adverbial and was not invented into a noun modifier.

R2.scope: Hanazono 2014, printed pp119–120 and following discussion: noun/particle syntax, commands, permission, negative existence, purpose and verb inflection. These constructions do not establish the full technical paragraph.

R3.scope: Named-supervisor municipal Okinawan prose independently uses とぅくま. This attests the word in Okinawan, not specifically every Shuri register.

R4.scope: Authored Okinawan grammar lesson by Higa Kiyoshi supplies とぅくる / とぅくま and nominal/location constructions. Supplementary firsthand usage, not the principal dictionary.

entries.note: Complete short label expresses exact position. Reconsidered after independently reading NINJAL entries ?aciraka (p102), hutasika (p224), tasika (p513), and saQkoo (p459), which explicitly use attributive -na with nouns. Thus な is an attested Okinawan construction, not sufficient evidence of Japanese substitution. 正確 is accepted here as a modern technical adjective-noun loan within that productive construction, with native とぅくま. Application of the attested construction to this modern loan is an inference; the exact label is not claimed as a dictionary quotation or native-speaker certification.

Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.

entries.note: All source clauses can be recovered, but later-imported 入れーたる is not supported by the cited put-in entry ?iri=juN (te-form ?iriti), and a Japanese 入れ stem cannot simply be assumed Okinawan. Repair that entire later-import/render clause with supported morphology, then rereview the full help value, including expansion/purpose and topic linkage. A possible research direction is いりたる for simple past attributive; this is not an accepted replacement. No issue is inferred solely from kanji spelling, and no semantic reversal of layer order was found.

review_history.note: The intended exact-position meaning is clear, but 正確な attaches the Japanese na-adjective ending directly to a native noun. A modern borrowing may be possible; the cited sources do not establish this attributive construction. No source-backed complete replacement is accepted by this review.
review_history.superseded_by: Direct primary dictionary evidence of attributive -na in the target language.
